subject: ss-medical-oncology
title: Infectious complications in oncology: neutropenic fever, opportunistic fungi, viral reactivation and vaccination principles

steps.tx: **Neutropenic fever** in cancer patients represents an acute medical emergency requiring emergent clinical evaluation. Paired blood cultures from all central venous line lumens and peripheral veins must be drawn prior to administering immediate empirical **broad-spectrum antibiotics** within 60 minutes of presentation to prevent lethal bacteremic shock and cardiovascular collapse.

steps.tx: **Invasive aspergillosis** is the leading lethal fungal killer in patients undergoing prolonged profound neutropenia and allogeneic stem cell transplantation. High-resolution chest computed tomography classically reveals early macronodules surrounded by ground-glass attenuation, termed **halo signs**, reflecting angioinvasive fungal ischemic infarction, progressing subsequently to late air-crescent cavitations during neutrophil recovery.

left.title: Early CT Halo Sign
points: Dense pulmonary nodule with ground-glass halo
Reflects fungal angioinvasion and surrounding hemorrhage

right.title: Late CT Air-Crescent Sign
points: Crescentic gas pocket within necrotic sequestrum
Reflects inflammatory cavitation and tissue retraction
Confirms healing or ongoing fungal cavitation

steps.tx: Paired scans contrast early **invasive aspergillosis** as a dense nodule ringed by **halo sign** ground glass bleed during deep neutropenia against later **air crescent** cavitation as neutrophils return. Reading halo as active vessel invasion and crescent as healing cavitation guides prompt antifungal start and follow up imaging in transplant and leukaemia hosts.
steps.say: The left scan shows a solid lung nodule wrapped in a soft grey halo of blood from fungus invading small vessels while counts are very low. The right scan shows the same area later opening into a crescent of air as infection walls off and white cells recover. Spotting the early halo should trigger fast antifungal therapy, while the later crescent signals cavitation and the need for continued care.

vis.alt: Paired lung scans show an early halo rimmed nodule and a later air crescent cavity.
vis.caption: Halo then crescent marks fungal invasion and healing. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Serum and **bronchoalveolar lavage** **galactomannan** antigen detection provides high sensitivity and specificity for the early diagnosis of invasive aspergillosis before definitive radiographic cavitation occurs. Serial optical density index monitoring enables preemptive antifungal therapy with voriconazole, significantly reducing mortality compared to empiric delayed approaches.

rows: Surveillance marker in profound prolonged neutropenia
Direct local assessment of lower respiratory fungal load
Pan-fungal cell-wall marker; detects Candida and Aspergillus, negative in Mucor

steps.tx: **Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole** **TMP-SMX** prophylaxis is mandatory for oncology patients receiving high-dose corticosteroids, fludarabine, or hyper-CVAD regimens to prevent lethal **Pneumocystis jirovecii** pneumonia. Standard dosing of one double-strength tablet three times weekly delivers complete alveolar protection, whereas atovaquone or inhaled pentamidine serve as validated alternatives for sulfa-allergic individuals.

rows: High-Dose Dexamethasone / Prednisone (>20 mg x 4 wk)
TMP-SMX 1 DS tablet oral 3 times weekly
Mitigates severe T-cell lymphopenia and opportunistic lung infection
Atovaquone 1500 mg daily or inhaled pentamidine 300 mg monthly

steps.tx: Universal **Hepatitis B virus** screening with surface antigen and total core antibody is mandatory prior to initiating rituximab, cytotoxic regimens, or stem cell transplantation. Administering prophylactic antiviral therapy with entecavir or tenofovir disoproxil prevents fatal fulminant **HBV reactivation** and catastrophic acute hepatic failure.

steps.tx: **Cytomegalovirus** reactivation is monitored with serial quantitative real-time PCR following allogeneic stem cell transplantation. Implementing scheduled **preemptive therapy** with oral valganciclovir or intravenous ganciclovir upon reaching predefined viral load thresholds arrests active replication and successfully prevents tissue-invasive cytomegalovirus pneumonitis, enteritis, and retinitis.

left.title: Preemptive Antiviral Strategy
points: Initiate valganciclovir 900 mg BID upon viral load trigger
Minimizes drug toxicity by targeting viremic patients

right.title: Primary Prophylaxis (Letermovir)
points: Dosed 480 mg daily from day 0 to day 100
Significantly reduces CMV reactivation without myelosuppression
Indicated in all CMV-seropositive allogeneic recipients

steps.tx: **Mucormycosis** is an aggressive, fulminant angioinvasive fungal infection seen in diabetic, acidotic, or neutropenic patients, presenting with reverse halo signs, dark necrotic eschars, and orbital invasion. Immediate treatment demands emergency surgical debridement of necrotic tissues coupled with high-dose **liposomal amphotericin B** at 5 to 10 mg/kg daily to forestall rapid vascular occlusion and death.

rows: Broad, non-septate or sparsely septate, right-angle (90 deg) branching
Reverse halo sign (central ground-glass with dense consolidation ring)
Classic halo sign (nodule with ground-glass rim)
Liposomal amphotericin B 5-10 mg/kg or isavuconazole
Voriconazole 6 mg/kg BID day 1, then 4 mg/kg BID

steps.tx: **Inactivated vaccines**, including recombinant seasonal influenza, conjugate pneumococcal, and recombinant zoster vaccines, are safe and recommended in oncology patients to bolster humoral immunity. Conversely, **live-attenuated** vaccines, such as measles-mumps-rubella, yellow fever, oral polio, and BCG, are strictly contraindicated during immunosuppressive chemotherapy due to fatal disseminated replication risks.
